cards.text: Israel's been camped in the Wilderness of Sinai, with God's cloud resting over the tabernacle, and the rule is simple: when the cloud stays, they stay, and when it lifts, they move. Then, on the twentieth day of the second month of the second year, the cloud lifts. Friend, this is the moment.

cards.question: The cloud lifts, and Israel sets out from the Wilderness of Sinai, traveling from place to place. Where does the cloud finally settle?

cards.text: This is the very first time the whole nation sets out like this, with Moses, Israel's leader, right there with them. I can't carry three trays across my bakery without one hitting the floor, and these folks are moving a whole NATION.

cards.question: Israel sets out from Sinai this first time because the tribe leaders decided it was time to go.

cards.text: Then they march out in order, camp by camp, each under its own standard. Judah goes first, then Reuben, then Ephraim, and Dan brings up the rear as the rear guard for everybody. Tucked in between, the Gershonites and Merarites carry the tabernacle, and the Kohathites carry the holy objects, so the tent is already standing by the time the holy things arrive.
Then Moses turns to Hobab, the son of Moses' father-in-law Reuel the Midianite. Israel is headed for the land the LORD said He would give them, and Moses wants Hobab to come along.

cards.question: Moses invites Hobab to come with Israel and says they'll treat him well. What reason does Moses give?

answers.text: The LORD has promised good things to Israel
The wilderness is too dangerous to cross alone
Hobab's own people have moved far away

cards.question: Hobab takes Moses up on the invitation right away.

cards.text: Hobab says he will not go. He's heading back to his own land and his own people, and Moses, the man leading a whole nation to a promised land, just got left on READ.

cards.question: Moses doesn't give up on Hobab. What does Moses say Hobab knows that Israel needs?

answers.text: Where they should camp in the wilderness
How to speak with the kings nearby
Which roads the enemy armies travel

cards.text: Moses says, "Please do not leave us," and tells Hobab he can serve as their eyes. A cloud in the sky AND a guy who knows the campsites, friend, and here I am needing a guide to find the sprinkles in my own pantry.

cards.question: Moses makes Hobab a promise: if he comes, Israel will ___ with him whatever good things the LORD gives them.

cards.text: Then they set out from the mountain of the LORD on a three-day journey. And something goes out in front of them the whole way.

cards.question: For those three days out from the mountain of the LORD, what travels ahead of Israel?
The ark of the covenant goes ahead of Israel for three days to seek a ___ place for them.
As Israel sets out from the camp, the cloud of the LORD is over them by day.
Whenever the ark of the covenant sets out ahead of Israel, Moses calls out to the LORD. What does he ask?

answers.text: For the LORD to rise up and scatter His enemies
For the LORD to make the road ahead smooth
For the LORD to send water to the camp

cards.text: His words: "Rise up, O LORD! May Your enemies be scattered; may those who hate You flee before You." Not once, friend, EVERY time that ark sets out, and I can't even remember to set my timer every time.
And whenever the ark comes to rest, Moses says, "Return, O LORD, to the countless thousands of Israel." Rise up when they march, return when they rest, and that's how Israel leaves Sinai.

findings.problem: The card states the cloud rule ('when the cloud stays, they stay, and when it lifts, they move'). That rule comes from Numbers 9:15-23, which is outside the passage. The card gives no reference for it and cites only Numbers 10:11, so the citation doesn't cover everything the card tells.

rule.text: Every fact and every verse number comes from that text. Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: Being 'left on READ' means getting no reply at all. Hobab does reply: he plainly says 'I will not go' (Numbers 10:30). The core action is being turned down, not being ignored, so the comparison doesn't match the fact.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'A pillar of fire' can be argued as right. Elsewhere in Scripture the pillar of fire goes before Israel by night (Exodus 13:21; Numbers 14:14), so a baker could argue it also travels ahead of them.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.
